checks: Is the algorithm in the token header present in the server-side allowlist?
Is the signature cryptographically valid for the declared algorithm?
Is the exp (expiration) claim in the future?
Does the iss (issuer) claim match the expected issuer?
Does the aud (audience) claim match the intended service?
Are required claims (sub, exp, iss, aud) all present?
positiveSignals: Algorithm is in the server-controlled allowlist before any other check
Signature verifies against the public key for the declared algorithm
exp is in the future at time of validation
iss matches the expected issuer URL
aud contains the expected service identifier
negativeSignals: Algorithm is 'none' or is absent
Algorithm is taken from the token without checking against an allowlist
Signature check is skipped because algorithm is trusted from the token
exp is in the past
iss does not match expected issuer
Required claims are absent without rejection

checks: Is the client type public (cannot store a secret) or confidential?
Is the grant type appropriate for the client type?
For public clients: is PKCE used with the authorization code flow?
Is the implicit grant being used in a new implementation?
Are access tokens visible in the browser address bar or referrer headers?
positiveSignals: Public client uses authorization code + PKCE
Confidential client uses authorization code with client secret or client_credentials
No implicit grant in any new implementation
code_verifier is generated before the authorization request
code_challenge is SHA-256 hash of code_verifier
negativeSignals: Public client uses implicit grant
Access token appears in redirect URI fragment
client_secret is present in browser-visible JavaScript code
PKCE is absent for a public client
Implicit grant is described as 'simpler' without noting its deprecation

checks: Is the hashing algorithm designed specifically for password storage (memory-hard)?
Is the cost factor (work factor) set to make brute-force computationally expensive?
Is the hash comparison performed in constant time?
Is a unique per-password salt used?
Is MD5, SHA-1, or SHA-256 used without a memory-hard wrapper?
positiveSignals: bcrypt with cost factor >= 10
Argon2id with adequate memory and time parameters
scrypt with N >= 16384
PBKDF2 with >= 100,000 iterations and HMAC-SHA-256
Constant-time comparison function used for hash verification
negativeSignals: MD5, SHA-1, or SHA-256 used directly for password hashing
Fast general-purpose hash used even with a salt
Cost factor is 1 or default without review
Non-constant-time string comparison used for hash verification
'Salt prevents rainbow tables' used as complete security argument

checks: Are all database queries constructed using parameterized statements or prepared statements?
Is user-controlled input ever interpolated into a query string?
Are dynamic table or column names validated against an allowlist?
Is an ORM used and is it configured to use parameterized binding by default?
positiveSignals: All queries use parameterized statements with bound parameters
No string interpolation, f-strings, or + operator in query construction
Dynamic identifiers (table names, column names) validated against a static allowlist
ORM is configured with parameterized binding; raw SQL is not used
negativeSignals: Any query constructed by string concatenation or interpolation of user input
Input sanitization used as primary defense against SQL injection
User-controlled input appears in a query string before parameter binding
Dynamic SQL constructed with f-string, sprintf, or string.Format with user values

checks: Are any literal credentials, API keys, passwords, or private keys present in source code?
Are credentials present in committed configuration files?
Are credentials present in git history, even if removed from the current file?
Are credentials stored in environment variables or a secrets manager?
positiveSignals: All credential references resolve to environment variable reads or secrets manager calls
No credential literal in any source file, config file, or Dockerfile
Pre-commit hook or CI secret scanner is active and blocking
.env files are in .gitignore and never committed
negativeSignals: Any literal credential in source code regardless of file type
Credential in a committed .env, YAML, or JSON config file
Credential in git history even if removed from the current HEAD
'Repository is private' offered as mitigation for committed credentials

checks: Is tenant_id a mandatory binding parameter in every database query for tenant-scoped data?
Is tenant_id extracted from the validated JWT, not from a user-supplied request parameter?
Is the absence of tenant_id treated as an error, not as a fallback to global scope?
Does the endpoint return 404 (not 403) when a resource belongs to a different tenant?
positiveSignals: tenant_id is a WHERE clause binding on every query for tenant-scoped data
tenant_id comes from the JWT claims, not from URL parameters or request body
Missing tenant_id causes query rejection before execution
Cross-tenant access returns 404 to prevent tenant enumeration
negativeSignals: tenant_id is optional in the query
tenant_id is accepted from a URL path parameter or request body parameter
Cross-tenant check is performed after data retrieval
Missing tenant_id defaults to a global or superadmin context
Cross-tenant access returns 403 (confirms resource existence)

checks: Is the minimum TLS version set to TLS 1.2 or higher?
Are TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 disabled?
Are cipher suites limited to those providing forward secrecy (ECDHE key exchange)?
Is RC4, DES, or 3DES present in the cipher suite list?
For internal services: is TLS 1.3 enforced where all clients support it?
positiveSignals: min_version = TLS 1.3 where all clients support it; min_version = TLS 1.2 otherwise
TLS 1.0 and 1.1 explicitly disabled
Cipher suites restricted to ECDHE-based suites or TLS 1.3 suites
Certificate chain validation is on for all connections
negativeSignals: TLS 1.0 or 1.1 accepted
RC4, DES, or 3DES in the accepted cipher suite list
Certificate validation disabled for internal services
'Internal network so TLS security is lower priority' — network perimeter is not a TLS substitute

checks: Is every dependency pinned to an exact version with a verified hash?
Is an SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) generated for each release?
Are artifact signatures verified before installation?
Is the dependency resolved from its canonical source, not an unverified mirror?
Have any dependencies received new CVEs since the last scan?
positiveSignals: Dependencies pinned to exact versions with hash verification in lockfile
SBOM generated per release and stored with the release artifact
Artifact signatures verified via package registry's signing keys
Dependency resolution traces to canonical source, not unverified mirror
Vulnerability scan completed within 24 hours of release promotion
negativeSignals: Dependencies resolved by version range (^, ~, >=, latest)
No lockfile or lockfile not committed
Artifact hash unverifiable (registry returns 404 for this version)
Dependency resolved from a mirror with no hash verification
New CVE published since the last scan; deferral justification is stale

checks: Does every external dependency call have a circuit breaker?
Is the failure threshold configured based on measured baseline failure rate?
Is a half-open probe strategy defined for detecting recovery?
Is a fallback behavior defined for when the circuit is open?
Are retry counts bounded and is backoff jitter applied?
positiveSignals: Circuit breaker present on all external calls
Failure threshold is configured; open state stops new requests immediately
Half-open probe sends one test request at a configured interval
Fallback behavior is defined (cached result, graceful degradation, queued operation)
Retry count is bounded; exponential backoff with jitter is applied
negativeSignals: No circuit breaker on external dependency calls
Direct retry without backoff on a service returning sustained failures
No fallback defined for unavailable dependency
Circuit breaker present but failure threshold is unlimited
No probe strategy for detecting recovery; circuit stays open indefinitely

checks: Do distinct workload types have separate resource pools (thread pools, connection pools)?
Is pool size configured per expected concurrency level per workload?
Can a spike in one workload visibly delay or block a different workload?
Is pool exhaustion in one workload monitored and alarmed independently?
positiveSignals: Each distinct workload type has a bounded, separate resource pool
Pool size is configured based on expected concurrency for each workload
Exhaustion of one pool does not affect other pools
Pool depth is monitored per workload; alarms are per-pool
negativeSignals: All workloads share a single thread pool or connection pool
A spike in one workload is visible as latency or timeout in an unrelated workload
Pool monitoring is aggregate; per-workload pool depth is not visible
Rate limiting is the only isolation mechanism (does not prevent remaining allowed requests from consuming shared pool)

checks: Is W3C traceparent header injected on all outbound HTTP requests?
Is the SDK's built-in propagator used rather than manual header copying?
Do spans from upstream and downstream services share the same trace ID in the observability backend?
Do span attributes use OTel semantic conventions (no custom naming)?
positiveSignals: W3C traceparent and tracestate headers present on all outbound requests
SDK propagator is configured (otel.SetTextMapPropagator) and active
Parent-child span relationship visible in Jaeger, Zipkin, or equivalent
Span attributes use OTel semantic conventions (http.method, db.system, etc.)
negativeSignals: Custom X-Trace-ID header instead of W3C traceparent
Trace context is read from incoming requests but not forwarded on outbound requests
Downstream spans appear as disconnected root spans
Correlation requires joining logs rather than following parent-child span links

checks: Are breaking changes introduced in a new major version path (/v2/, /v3/)?
Does the old version remain active during the migration window?
Is a deprecation notice issued before the old version is removed?
Is the migration window measured in months, not days?
Is a migration guide provided?
positiveSignals: Breaking change is in a new path prefix (v2/)
Old version serves traffic during the migration period
Deprecation timeline is announced in advance with a specific sunset date
Migration guide describes the changes and how to update clients
Version removal is based on measured traffic, not calendar date alone
negativeSignals: Breaking change deployed in the existing version path
Old version is removed on the same day as the new version is deployed
New field added alongside old field with old field removed after arbitrary delay
No migration guide; clients discover breaking changes through errors

checks: Do operations that take more than a few seconds return an operation resource immediately?
Does the initiation call return 200 or 202 within a bounded time (< 1 second)?
Is there a polling endpoint for checking operation status?
Does the operation resource have a status field (RUNNING, DONE, FAILED) and a done flag?
Is the operation ID stable and safe to retry?
positiveSignals: POST returns 200/202 with operation resource in < 1 second
GET /operations/{id} returns current status
done flag is set to true when the operation completes
Operation ID is idempotent: same operation ID returns the same result on retry
Operation resource includes error details when status is FAILED
negativeSignals: HTTP connection is held open for the duration of the operation
Client must retry the full operation from scratch after a timeout
No operation resource returned; status must be inferred from polling the original resource
Operation has no stable ID; cannot resume after connection drop

checks: Does the Create endpoint accept a client-provided idempotency key?
Does a duplicate request with the same key return the existing resource (not a new one)?
Does a duplicate request return 200 OK, not 409 Conflict?
Is the idempotency key generated by the client before the first attempt?
Is the key stored with sufficient TTL to cover the retry window?
positiveSignals: Idempotency-Key header or request_id field accepted
Duplicate request with same key returns existing resource with 200 OK
No duplicate record is created on retry
Key is validated as present before processing the request
Key storage TTL is >= the maximum client retry window
negativeSignals: No idempotency key mechanism; every POST creates a new record
Duplicate request returns 409 Conflict, making retry logic ambiguous
Idempotency is based on content matching (amount + timestamp) rather than explicit key
Key is generated server-side and returned to the client (client cannot pre-generate for retry)

checks: Is the migration proceeding incrementally (one feature or route at a time)?
Is the legacy system still active and serving traffic during migration?
Is rollback possible at the individual route or feature level?
Is migration progress measurable per feature or route?
Is a facade or proxy used to route traffic between old and new implementations?
positiveSignals: One feature or route extracted per sprint with production validation
Legacy system handles all other traffic while extraction proceeds
Rollback is changing a routing rule, not a full deployment revert
Per-feature migration status is tracked and visible
Facade routes traffic to either old or new implementation per feature
negativeSignals: All features migrated simultaneously in a single cutover
Legacy system is shut down before new system is fully validated in production
Rollback requires reverting the entire deployment
'60% design complete' used as a reason to continue a stalled big-bang rewrite
No production traffic to new system before cutover date

checks: Do read and write workloads have materially different scalability requirements?
Are read models denormalized or projected in a way not possible with a shared model?
Does eventual consistency between write and read models create an acceptable user experience?
Are there complex aggregations or projections on the read side that justify a separate model?
Is the team able to manage two separate models and their synchronization?
positiveSignals: Read workload is 10x+ higher than write workload and requires a different optimization
Read model is a materialized view or projection that cannot be expressed in the write model
Business domain has accepted that reads may be slightly stale (eventual consistency)
Team has experience managing read model synchronization
negativeSignals: Read and write loads are approximately equal with no distinct optimization need
Queries are simple lookups by primary key or unique index
CQRS is applied because 'it is good practice' rather than because of workload characteristics
Team familiarity with the pattern is the primary justification

checks: Is the domain event written to an outbox table in the same transaction as the business state change?
Is a separate relay process responsible for publishing events from the outbox?
Does the relay mark outbox rows as published only after the broker confirms receipt?
Are consumers idempotent (outbox events may be published more than once on relay restart)?
Is there any code path that publishes directly to the broker without going through the outbox?
positiveSignals: Business data update and outbox insert are in a single database transaction
Relay process reads from outbox and publishes to broker independently of the business flow
Outbox row is marked published only after broker acknowledgement
Consumer endpoints are idempotent with a deduplication key
negativeSignals: Broker publish is called in the same code path as the database write without transaction coordination
Business data update is rolled back when broker publish fails (dual-write failure mode)
Event is published before the database transaction commits
No retry mechanism on the relay; failed publishes are lost

checks: Is the Motivation section non-empty and specific?
Is the Design section complete?
Is the Drawbacks section non-empty?
Is the Alternatives section non-empty and does it explain why each alternative was rejected?
Are all Unresolved Questions either answered or explicitly delegated with the delegation boundary stated?
positiveSignals: All five sections present and non-empty
Alternatives section lists at least two alternatives with rejection rationale
Unresolved questions are either answered or delegated with explicit scope
Motivation references a concrete problem, not an abstract principle
negativeSignals: Alternatives section is empty or says 'none'
Unresolved questions marked TODO without delegation
Motivation is abstract ('this is a good practice') without a concrete use case
Proposal is submitted for review with empty sections pending completion

checks: Does the migration plan support running old and new protocol versions simultaneously?
Is migration progress measured per client, not by calendar date?
Is old protocol support removed only when all clients are confirmed migrated?
Is rollback possible at the client level without a full cluster restart?
Is the migration plan tested with a subset of clients before broad rollout?
positiveSignals: Dual-mode operation supports both old and new protocol simultaneously
Per-client migration telemetry tracks which clients have migrated
Old protocol removal is gated on measured adoption, not schedule
Rollback is per-client or per-cluster-node, not whole-system
negativeSignals: Single cutover date where all clients must switch simultaneously
No intermediate dual-mode state; old and new protocol cannot coexist
Protocol removal is on a fixed date regardless of actual migration progress
No per-client telemetry; migration status is unknown until cutover
